constraints.note: No per-run brief from Mike. Standing constraints applied: 5 topics, 8 clips = 5 fulls (1-5, by rank) + 3 impacts (6-8) for the three topics with a clear peak. All five topics are hype, project or conviction; no market-state clip was picked. Evaluation replay: the vertical master is not on disk, every timecode is from words.txt (word START times only, so each out-point is placed in the gap before the next word), and no segment ends after 3923 s (latest end is 2315.2).

topics.hook_summary: 'You got to get into assets now because this might be your last chance.' Robots get mass produced, every job gets completely wiped out, and the good news is you are on to crypto and you have a chance.
'I thought that we were just going to get like a 20x out of LAB.' It did 350x. Ten dollars into ten plays a week: one rugs, one does 300x, and the 300x more than makes up for it.
'Pieverse was one that I kept secret throughout pretty much the entire bear market.' He thinks it is good for multiple billions, much better than LAB, and LAB went to 7 billion.
'TAO isn't competing. It's the arena.' NEAR and Render qualify as one subnet under Bittensor, and TAO is going to give many, many multipliers.
'Good things cooking with Kaspa.' The KCC20 protocol is live, so now we can officially call them Kaspa tokens, the same way we say Solana tokens and ETH tokens, because they are on the L1.

clips.title: This Might Be Your Last Chance to Get Into Assets

segments.why: The named anchor: BlackRock launches its first active robotics ETF (RBTX). Starts on the second 'BlackRock' to skip the doubled read.
The thesis: the robotics narrative is going to be insane, for the whole economy and humanity; millions mass produced a year, more than cars.
COLD OPEN HOOK: 'you got to get into assets now because this might be your last chance.'
Why it is the last chance: normal things get so cheap that how the hell do you make extra money to invest.
The escalation starts: radiology completely wiped out, programming completely wiped out, AI now writes better code than us. Ends on 'right?' before the code-review tangent.

The run of 'completely wiped out' (software engineers, designers, actors, then electricians and plumbers when the robots hit the market), the driverless truck joke, and the payoff: you are on to crypto and you have a chance. We all have a chance.

peak_beats.note: 'You got to get into assets now because this might be your last chance.'
'When these guys hit the market, you're talking about electricians, plumbers, everybody completely wiped out.'
'The good news is you guys are on to crypto and you have a chance. We all have a chance.'

clips.notes: Emotional core (my read, text only): 645.85-716.4, the repeated 'completely wiped out' hammer that ends on 'you have a chance'. Assembly opens cold on the last-chance line, then backs up to BlackRock and the robotics thesis for context, then runs forward in stream order. Deliberately skipped: the entrepreneurial-mind ramble (568.0-587.7), the every-single-jobs video plug (587.9-600.5), the AI code-review tangent (630.6-645.5, off the crypto channel) and the yacht joke after the payoff (717.3-733.0, the end is tighter on 'we all have a chance'). Longest clip in the plan: if it needs to come down, the first trims are the BlackRock headline read (segment 0, a flat read) and the driverless truck aside (686.5-703.3 inside segment 5).

clips.title: We Thought LAB Was a 20x. It Did 350x

segments.why: The method and the receipts: 100 dollars a week, 10 dollars into ten plays, it adds up; some 50x, the 350x with LAB back in May, the 550x last September; long-term plays that go from a 20 million market cap to 7 billion. Closer of the short.
The spread of outcomes across his plays: a lot in the hundreds of Xs, a lot in the dozens, a lot single digit, a few rug. Ends on 'if one in 10 of my plays rugs,' BEFORE the ElizaOS mention.

The math that makes it work: if the highest performer is a 300x like LAB it more than makes up for it; one is the 300x, one rugs, the other eight still give you a 5x, a 10x, a 20x. Starts AFTER the ElizaOS mention.
COLD OPEN HOOK: 'I thought that we were just going to get like a 20x out of LAB. There's no way I thought we're going to go over 350x. I had no idea.'

peak_beats.note: 'Get a 300x, like a 350x with LAB we got back in May. We got the 550x last September. It happens, it happens.'
'I thought that we were just going to get like a 20x out of LAB... I had no idea.'
'20 million market cap, watch that bad boy pump to 7 billion, man.'

clips.notes: Scatter-gather across 33 minutes of stream (4:46, 35:01, 35:55, 38:20). Emotional core (my read): the 350x / 550x run at 308-322 and the LAB disbelief at 2300-2315. Order is hook (LAB surprise), then the portfolio math (one rugs, one does 300x, eight still multiply), then the practical method, ending on '20 million market cap... 7 billion, man'. The cash-out-and-rotate passage (336.2-368.5) is left out on purpose: fumbled delivery and rotation framing. ELIZAOS GUARD: the mention at 2139.8-2155.4 sits between segments 1 and 2 and must not leak into either join.

clips.title: I Kept This Coin Secret the Entire Bear Market

segments.why: What the project is, in one line: it is in the payments narrative but it is AI too, payments among agents.
COLD OPEN HOOK: 'Pieverse was one that I kept secret throughout pretty much the entire bear market up until recently.'

Why he trusts it: VCs and funding, not a degen play where you have no idea who is behind it and it could rug tomorrow; an 85 million market cap with funding is safer for a thousand dollars than a 100K market cap with an unknown dev.
The call: good for multiple billions, more than a 10x from 300 million, much better than LAB, and LAB went to 7 billion. Ends on 'right' before the trailing 'so we did some phenomenal gains'.
